articles.summary: Sunday's TBS Championship match between Maya World and Persephone during The Buy In pre-show of AEW's All In pay-per-view was interrupted by a highly anticipated return.
articles.body:
Sunday's TBS Championship match between Maya World and Persephone during The Buy In pre-show of AEW's All In pay-per-view was interrupted by a highly anticipated return.

During the closing moments of the match, a masked figure attacked World, allowing Persephone to pick up the win and claim the TBA title. After the match, the attacker took off her mask and was revealed to be former AEW Women's World Champion Britt Baker:

Baker hasn't been seen in AEW since her last match in November 2024. During the All In media call this past week, AEW CEO Tony Khan teased her potential return at the flagship PPV.

"Britt Baker is somebody who is an AEW original and has competed at All In London previously," Khan said at the time . "I know fans are always excited about Britt and asking about Britt. The last time we were in Wembley Stadium, Britt was on the show. I would say, as with all the questions about people returning or debuting, anytime we're getting asked about somebody coming back to AEW TV or debuting, I've always said, Stay tuned.' In this case, I would say that makes sense as well."

However, fans had the wind taken out of their sails on Friday when a report from Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News) revealed, "This should not be a surprise, but Britt Baker is not in London." It's now clear that AEW was able to keep her return under wraps for a massive surprise.

After winning the TBS title to go along with her CMLL Women's Championship, Persephone made her alliance with Baker official and targeted Thunder Rosa in a backstage interview:

Baker's return adds even more intrigue to the AEW women's division, which is already filled with impressive talent and exciting storylines.

articles.title: AEW All In 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: AEW returned to Wembley Stadium Sunday for its All In pay-per-view extravaganza, headlined by London's native son, Will Ospreay, challenging Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
AEW returned to Wembley Stadium Sunday for its All In pay-per-view extravaganza, headlined by London's native son, Will Ospreay, challenging Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.

Did the Aerial Assassin pay off his arduous journey, including neck surgery, and win the title in front of his family and friends, or did Omega once again prove to be the hurdle he cannot overcome?

Find out the answer to that and more in this recap, including grades and analysis for each of the card's bouts.

AEW World Championship Match: Kenny Omega (c) vs. Will Ospreay

AEW World Women's Championship Match: Willow Nightingale (c) vs. Mercedes Mone

AEW World Tag Team Championship Match: Cope and Christian Cage (c) vs. The Young Bucks

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship Match: The Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion (c)

AEW International Championship Match: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kyle Fletcher (c) vs. Kazuchika Okada

Falls Count Anywhere Match for the TNT Championship: Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight (c)

Continental Challenge Cup Final for the Continental Championship: Nigel McGuinnes vs. Jon Moxley (c)

Casino Gauntlet Match: Andrade El Idolo vs. MJF vs. Tommaso Ciampa vs. More to be announced

Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championship: Hangman Page and Brodido (c) vs. The Death Riders vs. The Demand vs. The Bang Bang Gang vs. The Conglomeration vs. The Dogs

TBS Championship Match: Maya World (c) vs. Persephone

8-Man Tag Team Match: The Hurt Business, Big Boom AJ, and QT Marshall vs. Shane Taylor Promotions

Harley Cameron and Kris Statlander vs. Skye Blue and Julia Hart

The Rascalz and Lio Rush defeated Action Andretti, Hook, Anthony Bowens, and Katsuyori Shibata

A fun, energetic match that highlighted both teams, especially the popular Rush, this was a great tone-setter as fans continued to arrive at the stadium. The babyfaces went over, too, with the look on Andretti's face after the match suggesting that he and Rush are headed toward a showdown over his Ring of Honor Television Championship.

Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron defeated Skye Blue and Julia Hart

This was a short, formulaic match featuring Cameron fighting from underneath before making the tag that decided the outcome. Statlander proved the difference as she drove Hart down with Saturday Night Fever for the win. Statlander and Cameron are very popular, but the Triangle of Madness is a legitimate team that would have benefited from winning here.

The Hurt Business and Doom and Boom defeated Shane Taylor Promotions

A high-energy bout down the stretch showcased all eight competitors and had the fans more invested than they were earlier in the bout. The babyfaces predictably went over, with Lashley putting Charlie Bravo down with the Dominator for the win. There was an interesting booking decision late, with Trish Adora and Christyan XO distracting Bryce Remsburg, which allowed Big Justice to interfere and join his dad for a double spear spot. They remained on the apron when it was clearly hurting their charges, which made little sense.

TBS Championship Match: Persephone defeated Maya World to win the title

A good, competitive match, but it never had the audience completely invested as one would hope given the recent stature of both women on AEW TV. This was a solid showing by World, but her opponent stood out, thanks to her in-ring work and the ability to tell the match's story through facial expressions and body language.

Late in the match, a masked and hooded individual shoved the It Girl from the top rope, allowing Persephone to win the match and the title. After the match, Dr. Britt Baker revealed herself to be under the mask in the night's first big moment, of which there are expected to be several.

Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championship

Order of entry: Bang Bang Gang, The Dogs, The Demand, The Conglomeration, The Death Riders, Hangman Page and Brodido, Swerve Strickland and The New Level

Austin Creed and Kofi took things to a New Level Sunday in London, arriving in AEW as the partners of Swerve Strickland in the Trios Roulette Royale to a thunderous ovation.

Their arrival was only one highlight of a match that featured several stories and rivalries intertwined throughout, including that of the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs, as well as Strickland and Page. The elimination of the latter by Ricochet guaranteed new champions.

Strickland and New Level would pay off their debut outing by eliminating the competition and claiming the titles, capping off an excellent match that started slowly, with too many wrestlers in the ring at once, but improved with every passing minute, culminating in a crowd-pleasing moment and a career-defining one for Creed and Kofi.

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship Match: Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion

Last Time in Action: Divine Dominion and Persephone defeated Maya World and The Brawling Birds (Dynamite, August 26)

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross faced the toughest test of their reign as champions on Sunday, battling England's own Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor in the main show's opening contest.

The heels isolated Hayter early, wearing her down in their corner of the ring. A pair of clotheslines allowed the former world champion to fend off the champions and make the tag to Windsor, who spurred the babyface comeback.

As the action rolled on, each team took turns unloading their arsenals, neither able to keep the other down. The heels teed off on Hayter, driving her to the mat with a double chokeslam, but Windsor broke up the pin.

The challengers survived the punishing offense of their dominant opponents and finished Kross off with Two Birds, One Stone for the win and the titles.

This was a strong match with some great tag team work from both teams and a finish that saw the right team take the titles.

Hayter and Windsor beat the seemingly unbeatable, but who of the other teams in the division stand a realistic shot at dethroning them?

The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion to win the titles

Kross and Bayne are a success story as a team thrown together that managed to develop into a great tandem, with strong chemistry, who carried the women's tag division on their backs for five months.

Hayter and Windsor getting the home country win was a great moment for them and pays off what has been a string of great performances. They could be the anchor piece for the division moving forward.

Continental Cup Final for the AEW Continental Championship: Nigel McGuinness vs. Jon Moxley

Last Time in Action: Jon Moxley defeated Claudio Castagnoli (Dynamite, August 26); Nigel McGuinness defeated Kyle O'Reilly (Dynamite, August 26)

The AEW Continental Championship and victory in this year's Continental Challenge Cup tournament were on the line as London's own Nigel McGuinness battled Jon Moxley in the second match of the main card.

Moxley targeted his opponent's lower leg and ankle while McGuinness worked over his opponent's left arm. The challenger flattened the champion with a Tower of London, rocked his opponent with a tandem of lariats, then escaped the bulldog choke and applied the London Dungeon submission hold.

None of it was enough to keep the Death Rider down or force a tapout.

Instead, Moxley absorbed everything thrown at him by the former Ring of Honor world champion and trapped him in an ankle lock. McGuinness showed tremendous grit and toughness as he fought through the pain to come within an inch of the ropes, only for the suffering to be too great to overcome. He tapped out, awarding the match and the Continental Cup to Moxley.

The best match of the night to this point, it featured some excellent grappling from McGuinness, and Moxley looked competent wrestling that style of match. He may not be the great worker that some believe him to be, but outwrestling McGuinness in Wembley is an enormous feat. Hanging with the measuring stick for toughness in AEW is a testament to the runner-up, too.

Moxley defeated McGuinness to retain the title

Moxley survived a Tower of London before trading LeBelle Locks with his opponent, all while Bryan Danielson called the action on commentary, in a nice ode to the former world champion.

McGuinness countered a sunset flip, stacking Moxley high on his shoulders in an homage to Bret Hart vs. British Bulldog from SummerSlam 1992, a match the challenger watched in the same Wembley Stadium as a child. A great callback.

AEW International Championship Match: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada vs. Kyle Fletcher

Last Time in Action: Kyle Fletcher defeated Mike Bailey (Dynamite, August 5); Kazuchika Okada, Hechicero, and Kevin Knight lost to Corazon de Leon, Darby Allin, and Mistico (Dynamite, August 5); Konosuke Takeshita defeated The Beast Mortos (Collision, August 26)

"Protostar" Kyle Fletcher defended the AEW International Championship against "Rainmaker" Kazuchika Okada and Konosuke Takeshita in a Three-Way Dance.

The Don Callis Family further disintegrated when two miscommunications led to Okada and Fletcher taking each other out. The latter followed with a lariat of his own to The Rainmaker, resulting in Callis noting on commentary, "We're all sportsmen in the Don Callis Family."

Takeshita delivered a Powerdrive Knee to Fletcher, followed by Raging Fire, but Okada broke up the pin and landed the Rainmaker to his former partner-turned-enemy. Fletcher broke that pin up to save his title reign.

Moments later, Fletcher fired up, brought Takeshita from the top rope and appeared to be on his way to victory. Instead, Okada appeared and flattened his DCF stablemate with the Rainmaker to win the match and the title.

After the match, Fletcher awarded Okada the title, then reluctantly raised the victor's hand.

This a predictably great match. The talent involved nearly guaranteed as much. Fletcher continued to showcase the skills that have made him the brightest young star in AEW. Ditto, Takeshita.

The finish was interesting in that Okada distinctly chose to pin Fletcher, even though he easily could have pinned the other opponent. His actions after the match, demanding The Protostar raise his hand, make one think that Fletcher may be on his way out of the faction.

Okada defeated Fletcher and Takeshita to win the title

Fletcher hit the ring dressed as Donquixote Doflamingo from One Piece . Great pop culture reference and one that fit his pink color scheme.

Takeshita followed Okada up, then delivered a bridging German suplex to Fletcher, for a creative double-pin spot.

Okada is delightful as the grinning, disingenuous, braggadocios villain.

Casino Gauntlet Match to Determine the No. 1 Contender

Order of Entry: Andrade El Idolo, MJF, Nick Wayne, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Tommaso Ciampa, Chris Jericho, Mark Davis, Komander, Mistico, Daniel Garcia , Jungle Jack Perry

Andrade El Idolo earned a future shot at the AEW World Championship by way of his win in the Casino Gauntlet Match Sunday in London.

He overcame an early battle with rival MJF, as well as the arrivals of former world champions and young stars with plenty to prove, to capture the title in an entertaining match. Still, it lacked the overall quality of other matches of its kind.

One thing the contest did do was play up the idea that if a fall was scored before all competitors could enter the ring, those wrestlers would miss out on an opportunity to compete for the top prize in the company.

That is exactly what happened, according to the commentary team, as El Idolo delivered MJF's Heat Seeker to Nick Wayne for the win and title shot.

Some will argue this could have been better served as a one-on-one match between Andrade and MJF and while they may have a point, this format allowed one to win without the other suffering an unnecessary loss. Even better? That singles match can take place at a later date, on a show where it will not be overshadowed by other main events.

The unannounced time intervals allowed for more unpredictability and creative convenience. It also felt cheap in that it adapted the rules to fit the stories AEW wanted to tell rather than the other way around.

This might have been the most inconsequential appearance by Jericho on an AEW pay-per-view ever.

The meteoric rise of El Idolo in this return to AEW has been refreshing for his fans, who did not have a lot to be excited about in the last handful of years.

articles.title: New Day's Kofi Kingston, Xavier Woods Win AEW Titles as New Level in Debut at All In After WWE Exit
articles.summary: After a 12-year run as a team in WWE, New Day's Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their AEW debut Sunday at All In as New Level under the names Kofi and Awesome Austin Creed.
articles.body:
After a 12-year run as a team in WWE, New Day's Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their AEW debut Sunday at All In as New Level under the names Kofi and Awesome Austin Creed.

Kofi and Creed emerged at Wembley Stadium in London as the surprise tag team partners for Swerve Strickland in the AEW Trios Roulette Royale.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Swerve, Kofi and Creed won the match to dethrone "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido as AEW World Trios Champions. Kofi and Creed are now the first AEW wrestlers to win a title in their first appearance in the company.

The professional wrestling world was left in a state of shock in May when Kingston and Woods left WWE after 20 and 16 years with the company, respectively.

It was later reported by Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News) that Kingston and Woods made the decision to leave WWE after being asked to take a pay cut.

When Kingston and Woods officially became free agents 90 days after their WWE release, they posted an animated video on X that seemed to indicate they had left WWE and were preparing to write their next chapter in pro wrestling:

For most of its existence, New Day was a three-man unit comprised of Kingston, Woods and Big E in WWE. In any iteration, New Day is the most-decorated tag team in WWE history with 12 tag team title reigns, including a record for the longest singular reign at 483 days.

When Big E suffered a serious neck injury in 2022 that rendered him unable to wrestle any longer, Kingston and Woods continued to use the New Day moniker as a duo.

Individually, the 45-year-old Kingston was a four-time intercontinental champion and three-time United States champion. He also won the WWE Championship at WrestleMania 35 in one of the most memorable moments in WrestleMania history.

Woods, 39, never held a singles title in WWE, but he did win the 2021 King of the Ring tournament.

With Kingston and Woods now in AEW, they figure to become a featured part of an already stacked tag team division that includes The Young Bucks, Cope and Cage, FTR, The Motor City Machine Guns and many others.

articles.title: Brawling Birds Beat Divine Dominion to Win AEW Women's Tag Titles at All In 2026 at Wembly
articles.summary: The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion at All In 2026 on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships at Wembley Stadium in London.
articles.body:
The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion at All In 2026 on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships at Wembley Stadium in London.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross entered All In as the longest-reigning AEW women's tag team champions in the brief history of the titles, as they had held them since March.

Divine Dominion beat the inaugural titleholders, Willow Nightingale and Harley Cameron, at the Revolution pay-per-view, and they were champions for over five months by the time All In rolled around.

After winning the championships, Bayne and Kross ran through many of the top women's tag teams AEW has to offer, including Kris Statlander and Hikaru Shida, Tay Melo and Anna Jay, and Julia Hart and Skye Blue.

Arguably the one notable team that Divine Dominion could not solve was The Brawling Birds, as Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor teamed with Willow to beat Bayne, Kross and Mercedes Moné in a six-woman tag team match on Dynamite earlier this month.

Following that bout, Hayter and Windsor against Bayne and Kross for the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships was made official for All In.

The Brawling Birds were a fitting choice to oppose Divine Dominion because of the added meaning that came along with All In being held in London.

Both Hayter and Windsor are from England, giving them a distinct home-field advantage over Bayne and Kross, who are from the United States and Australia, respectively.

While Bayne and Kross undoubtedly had the size and strength edge, Hayter and Windsor had the benefit of being able to draw inspiration from the large crowd that packed into Wembley.

With the London faithful cheering them on, The Brawling Birds ended Divine Dominion's lengthy title reign and became the third women's tag team champs in AEW history.

articles.title: Jon Moxley Beats Nigel McGuinness to Retain AEW Continental Title at All In 2026 at Wembley
articles.summary: Jon Moxley beat Nigel McGuinness in McGuinness' hometown of London at AEW All In on Sunday to retain the Continental Championship.
articles.body:
Jon Moxley beat Nigel McGuinness in McGuinness' hometown of London at AEW All In on Sunday to retain the Continental Championship.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Sunday's bout was the culmination of the Continental Challenge Cup, which saw 16 AEW stars compete for the opportunity to have a continental title match at All In.

Despite holding the Continental Championship since December, Mox was included in the tourney, meaning he would have to run the table in order to keep the title in his possession.

Moxley impressively made his way to the finals by beating Jack Perry in the first round and Jay White in the quarterfinals before getting the better of Death Riders stablemate Claudio Castagnoli in the semis.

At 50 years of age, McGuinness was the oldest participant in the tournament, but he was a sentimental favorite due to the possibility of him getting to have a big match in his home country of England at All In.

McGuinness quickly went from an underdog to a true title contender by beating Katsuyori Shibata in the first round, Hechicero in the quarterfinals and Kyle O'Reilly in the semifinals.

With that, McGuinness' ticket was punched to Wembley Stadium and his biggest match since returning to the squared circle two years ago.

McGuinness ended a 13-year absence from in-ring competition at All In 2024 by taking part in the Casino Gauntlet, and it was fitting that his match against Moxley happened at the same venue.

While McGuinness' return has been a great story in pro wrestling, a one-on-one match against arguably the most successful wrestler in AEW history at All In was an entirely different challenge than anything else he has faced the past two years.

Although McGuinness looked like he belonged on Sunday, Mox denied him what would have been the first title win of his AEW career.

articles.title: Okada Beats Fletcher, Takeshita to Win AEW International Title at All In 2026 at Wembley
articles.summary: Kazuchika Okada beat Kyle Fletcher and Konosuke Takeshita in a three-way match at AEW All In on Sunday to win the International Championship.
articles.body:
Kazuchika Okada beat Kyle Fletcher and Konosuke Takeshita in a three-way match at AEW All In on Sunday to win the International Championship.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Okada had the chance to pin Takeshita, but he chose to pin Fletcher, likely setting up a rivalry between the two Don Callis Family members.

After winning the International Championship for the first time last month, Fletcher was almost instantly met with a massive challenge for All In.

In Okada and Takeshita, Fletcher had to face the two wrestlers who held the international title immediately before him.

While a rematch with Takeshita was expected after Fletcher beat him for the International Championship at the Beach Break edition of Dynamite, Okada's inclusion was a bit of a curveball.

Don Callis, who manages both Fletcher and Okada, broke the news to Fletcher, theorizing that adding another member of The Don Callis Family to the match would give them a better chance of keeping the title in the stable.

Takeshita, who is a former member of The Don Callis Family, made his AEW return on the Aug. 19 episode of Dynamite after being away from the company for over a month in order to compete in New Japan Pro-Wrestling's G1 Climax tournament.

The Alpha interrupted a Don Callis Family meeting that saw Fletcher and Okada agree to work together at All In to ensure that Takeshita would not win back the international title.

Takeshita attacked Fletcher and left him laying due to the fact that Okada bailed rather than lending his stablemate a helping hand.

Because of that, there was plenty of tension between Fletcher and Okada entering All In, and no guarantee that they would be on the same page.

Even so, Okada rose to the occasion on the big stage and defeated both Fletcher and Takeshita to become a two-time international champion.

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer admits Chantelle Cameron's trash talk 'triggered' her as American expresses regret for post-fight antics
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer says she "acted in a way that I shouldn't have" after Saturday's defeat to Chantelle Cameron in Birmingham; the American has accepted the decision a day after claiming victory in the ring; a rematch clause is in the contract with Mayer open to three-minute rounds
articles.body:
The defeat was just the third of Mayer's professional career and cost her the unified belts she had brought to Birmingham, a breathless contest between two of the sport's pound-for-pound elite living up to its billing and strengthening Cameron's claim to a place among the greats of the women's game.

The pair had to be separated by security after a physical altercation at Friday's weigh-in and clashed again in the ring on Saturday night, with Mayer telling the new unified WBA, WBC and WBO champion "I did beat you" after the judges scored it 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 against her.

Speaking to Sky Sports News , Mayer said: "In the heat of the moment after the fight, I felt I had won, but I knew it was close, and I was prepared to go to the mic and give her her props and say I'm looking forward to the rematch.

"I'm not going to lie, I heard her on the mic talking trash and it triggered me. It brought something out of me and I feel like I acted in a way that I shouldn't have."

Mayer also traced the rivalry's flashpoint back to what happened in the build-up.

"We were always actually really cool, and the only thing that kind of triggered that rivalry was me getting in her face during the face-off," she said, suggesting Cameron may have "had all those words to say" about her "deep down".

Cameron, who admitted she had "genuinely respected" Mayer before the build-up soured, believes the hostility rebounded on the American.

"I was looking at her before the bell rang and thought, 'I'm going to smash your head in'," said Cameron after the fight. "And it worked. I was feeling the energy, she didn't want to be in there."

The contest exacted a toll befitting its billing, both fighters visibly swollen by the ninth round with Mayer cut by the eye and Cameron bleeding from hers, and the two embraced at the final bell before the verbal hostilities resumed.

A day on from disputing the verdict, Mayer struck a markedly different tone.

"I have not watched the fight back, but I am open to the idea that it was too close," she said. "I told myself I would not let the fight get close, and I didn't do that. I let it get too close, and so I can't be upset at the decision.

"It wasn't my night, and I have to give her the props for the win. She's a great fighter, and I'm just excited to go fix my mistakes and do better."

Victory further burnished a Cameron CV that already carried the only professional defeat inflicted on Katie Taylor, although the Briton played down talk of being the greatest of all time, insisting Claressa Shields still holds that mantle.

Rematch 'in the contract' with three-minute rounds on the table

Mayer confirmed a rematch clause exists and that she expects it to be activated.

The American also revealed she had declined to give up her WBC belt to make Saturday's fight three-minute rounds, and says the choice now rests with the new champion.

"I don't see a way that it doesn't happen because it's in the contract," she said. "We both want it and we'll make it happen.

"I wasn't willing to vacate my WBC belt in order to go three-minute rounds. In order to go three-minute rounds, I had to vacate that WBC belt but I know how much the belts play a role in your negotiation.

"She has the belts and she wants to go three-minute rounds. We can absolutely do that. I have no problem with that. It's her choice now, just like it was my choice for this fight."

Cameron made three-minute rounds her condition in the immediate aftermath of the dramatic victory.

"I want to do this again," she said on Saturday night. "It's up to Mikaela, but I want to do three-minute rounds."

Her coach Jamie Moore also said the champion could vacate the WBC belt if the sanctioning body refuses.

MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian welcomed a second meeting while revealing Cameron has pushed for fights with Claressa Shields and Lauren Price "from the jump".

He also insisted that the 35-year-old Brit is "unequivocally" among the top two or three female fighters of all time, if not the greatest.

Mayer, who on Saturday had insisted any rematch must happen in the United States, made no mention of venue and instead paid tribute to the UK fans.

"I love you guys, I can't wait to come back. I'm here for your entertainment," she added.

articles.title: Cage & Cope Beat Young Bucks in Dream Match to Retain AEW Tag Titles at All In 2026
articles.summary: Adam Copeland and Christian Cage beat The Young Bucks at All In on Sunday to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championships.
articles.body:
Adam Copeland and Christian Cage beat The Young Bucks at All In on Sunday to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championships.

Cage hit Matt Jackson with a wrench before hitting his finisher, but the referee didn't see the illegal blow:

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

After the match, Cage and Copeland were confronted by fellow legendary tag teams FTR, the Motor City Machine Guns and the New Level, the latter of whom debuted in AEW earlier in the event and won the Trios Championship alongside Swerve Strickland.

After about six months off AEW programming, Cope and Cage returned at Revolution in March, and they seemingly lent The Young Bucks a helping hand by running off FTR.

However, it proved to be a measure of revenge more than anything, as Copeland and Christian wanted to get back at FTR after an attack at their hands last September.

After getting some payback against FTR, Cope and Cage stared down The Young Bucks, which served to foreshadow their eventual showdown at All In.

Copeland and Cage defeated FTR in an "I Quit" street fight at Double or Nothing, marking their first reign as AEW world tag team champions together after previously holding tag team gold as a duo seven times in WWE.

At Redemption, both The Young Bucks and the team of Cope and Cage had huge matches that led to their title bout becoming official for All In.

The Young Bucks beat the team of Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay at the event, and Copeland and Christian later defeated Death Riders members Claudio Castagnoli and Pac to retain the tag team titles.

After Cope and Cage were victorious, The Young Bucks made their way to the ring to confront them, and the graphic for the AEW World Tag Team Championship match between them at All In was shown on the big screen, much to the delight of the live crowd.

At Wembley Stadium in London, two of the most accomplished and celebrated tag teams in pro wrestling history finally locked horns for the first time ever.

Cope and Christian came out on top, denying The Young Bucks what would have been a record-breaking fourth reign as AEW world tag team champions.

articles.title: Darby Allin Beats Kevin Knight to Win AEW TNT Title in Falls Count Anywhere Match at All In 2026
articles.summary: Darby Allin beat Kevin Knight in a Falls Count Anywhere match to win the TNT Championship at AEW All In 2026 in London on Sunday.
articles.body:
Darby Allin beat Kevin Knight in a Falls Count Anywhere match to win the TNT Championship at AEW All In 2026 in London on Sunday.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

After the Don Callis Family interfered on Knight's behalf, Allin got an assist from his mentor, Sting, and Sting's son, Steven Borden.

The rivalry between Knight and Allin began at Double or Nothing back in May, following the main event, which saw Allin drop the AEW World Championship to MJF.

Knight showed up after the match in an apparent attempt to attack MJF and protect Allin, but The Jet turned his attention to Allin instead and turned heel by hitting Allin with a UFO Splash.

A couple of weeks later, Allin got some measure of revenge by hitting Knight with a skateboard, which led to a TNT title match between them on the July 22 episode of Dynamite.

Knight won the match to retain the title, but it was far from convincing, as Knight hit Allin with the TNT Championship belt while the referee was incapacitated, which led directly to the victory.

Given the controversial nature of that contest, Allin was granted a rematch for All In, but this time it came along with Falls Count Anywhere rules, ensuring that Knight and Allin would be on equal footing.

While the Knight vs. Allin feud was already heated, it reached a fever pitch during the Aug. 19 edition of Dynamite when Knight set a trap that Allin fell right into.

Knight called Allin out to the ring for a confrontation, but when Allin made it to the ramp, he found himself engulfed in a storm of pyro.

With Allin injured and out of sorts, Knight brought him to the ring and hit him with a Coast to Coast that saw Allin get smashed in the face with a steel chair.

Allin was out for payback at All In, and he got it by defeating Knight and becoming a record-tying, three-time TNT champion in the process.

articles.title: Mercedes Mone Beats Willow Nightingale to Win AEW Women's Title at All In 2026 at Wembley
articles.summary: Mercedes Moné defeated Willow Nightingale at All In at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Championship for the first time.
articles.body:
Mercedes Moné defeated Willow Nightingale at All In at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Championship for the first time.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

While a showdown between Mercedes and Willow at All In long felt inevitable, the manner in which they got there was somewhat unexpected.

Nightingale was originally slated to compete in the 2026 Owen Hart Cup tournament with the winner earning the right to challenge for the AEW women's world title at All In.

However, due to injury, Willow had to pull out of the tourney. Her surprise replacement was Moné, who made her return to AEW programming after a hiatus of more than five months.

Mercedes went on to win the Owen Hart Cup for the second straight year, beating Maya World in the finals at Forbidden Door.

Nightingale returned to action shortly thereafter and won a Casino Gauntlet Match on the July 8 episode of Dynamite to earn an AEW Women's Championship match against Thekla at Redemption.

Willow took down Thekla at Redemption, finally winning her first AEW women's world title in the process.

That set the stage for Nightingale vs. Moné at All In, and it was a fitting title match given the history they have built together in recent years.

In Mercedes' first AEW match, she beat Willow for the TBS Championship in 2024, but Willow later beat Mercedes for the TBS Championship in the final match before Moné's AEW hiatus in December 2025.

They did battle once again Sunday at All In, and Mercedes was victorious this time around, allowing her to finally reach the top of the mountain in the AEW women's division.

articles.title: Moses Itauma says he will "be back" after world-title defeat by Filip Hrgovic
articles.summary: Great Britain's Moses Itauma says he will "be back" after failing in his attempt to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion.
articles.body:
Moses Itauma vowed "I'll be back" after failing in his attempt to become the second-youngest ever heavyweight world champion on Saturday.

Britain's Itauma, 21, tore through his first 14 opponents but his team threw in the towel in the ninth round against Filip Hrgovic at O2 Arena, London.

Having appeared to punch himself out, Itauma was barely able to stand as Hrgovic, 34, applied pressure to end the fight.

"It wasn't my night, we attempted greatness and just fell short to the more experienced man," Itauma said on social media.

"I want to say congratulations to Filip Hrgovic on his win. And although I never reached my desired outcome, I believe I gained experience that I'll take to my future fights.

"God bless, take care and I'll be back."

Heavyweight Itauma handed harsh world-title lesson

The vacant IBF title was on the line and Itauma was the favourite heading into the fight.

Hrgovic - who has lost only one professional fight, to Daniel Dubois in 2024 - is known for his durability, but he struggled to keep pace with Itauma early on.

However, his experience eventually told as the Briton was forced to leave the arena on a stretcher.

He was then taken to hospital and released overnight after having precautionary medical checks.

Queensberry Promotions boss Frank Warren believes Itauma needs a tactical rethink if he is to reach the top.

"That aura of invincibility, at the moment, is gone," Warren said. "People will look at that and maybe it will make it easier to make fights for him.

"He's still one of the most unbelievable talents I've ever been involved with. We'll stick with him. He needs a bit more ring craft and needs to stop thinking about knocking everyone out."

articles.title: Will Ospreay Beats Kenny Omega to Win AEW Title at All In 2026 at Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: Will Ospreay defeated Kenny Omega in the main event of All In at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday to win the AEW World Championship for the first time.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay defeated Kenny Omega in the main event of All In at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday to win the AEW World Championship for the first time.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Ospreay and Omega put together another instant classic full of highlights, but in the end, the Englishman brought the title home in front of his countrymen.

Ospreay became the No. 1 contender and earned the right to challenge for the AEW world title in his hometown of London at Forbidden Door in June when he beat Swerve Strickland in the finals of the Owen Hart Cup tournament.

While Ospreay's title match was locked in for All In with that victory, it wasn't yet known who his opponent would be.

MJF was the AEW world champion at the time, but he was tasked with putting the title on the line against Omega on the July 8 episode of Dynamite. Omega beat MJF to become a two-time AEW world champ, setting the stage for Omega vs. Ospreay at All In.

However, Omega first had to defend the title against Kevin Knight in the main event of Redemption last month, and he did so successfully despite Knight pushing him to the limit.

After the match, The Death Riders attacked Omega, but Ospreay made his way to the ring in order to protect his All In opponent.

Ospreay had been working with The Death Riders in the weeks and months leading up to Redemption, as they were helping him find his killer instinct en route to vying for the AEW World Championship.

Despite his relationship with The Death Riders, Ospreay declined Jon Moxley's urging to put a plastic bag over Omega's head, and he cleared Mox out of the ring.

Even though Ospreay saved him, Omega hit Ospreay with a One Winged Angel, signaling that he would not go quietly at All In.

After weeks of back-and-forth between them on the mic, Omega and Ospreay finally settled the score inside the ring on Sunday, and it ended with Ospreay becoming AEW world champion.

articles.title: MJF, Will Ospreay, Real Winners and Losers of AEW All In 2026 Match Card
articles.summary: AEW's biggest show of the year was once again one of their best of 2026 so far as All In delivered in spades from Wembley Stadium in London.
articles.body:
AEW's biggest show of the year was once again one of their best of 2026 so far as All In delivered in spades from Wembley Stadium in London.

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay's highly-anticipated main event was the focal point of the pay-per-view, but the rest of the card featured its fair share of marquee matches with multiple title changes and memorable moments.

The event also effectively set the stage for the months to come with Andrade El Idolo earning an opportunity at the AEW World Championship and The New Level making their heavily-rumored debuts in the tag team ranks.

Names who played a pivotal role in previous installments of All In either fell under the radar this year or emerged as afterthoughts. Some outcomes were predictable yet satisfactory, while others were surprising and questionable.

These are the real winners and losers of AEW All In 2026.

The star of an otherwise uneventful All In pre-show was the returning Britt Baker, who had not been seen on AEW TV in nearly two years.

Her last major match came at All In 2024 in a loss to then-AEW TBS champion Mercedes Moné. She resurfaced once again getting involved in TBS title business, targeting Maya World following her loss of the prestigious prize to Persephone.

Just as it looked like Baker was on her way out of the company and potentially headed to WWE, Baker made her presence felt in AEW and instantly reestablished herself as a player in the division. She automatically adds interest to the title picture and gives World a notable name to work with now that she's no longer champ.

Although it occurred on the pre-show, Baker's return was well executed and served as a nice surprise. Now the key is ensuring she can regain the relevance she once had.

The same man who not only headlined but won last year's All In main event for the AEW World Championship wound up opening this year's installment in a bloated AEW World Trios Championship gauntlet-style match.

Adam Page won the Trios titles only earlier this month with Brodido after being away for the better part of four months. His inability to fight for the company's top title forced him into a rather random spot that seemed like an excuse to get him (and other equally-directionless stars) on the card.

There were glimmers of greatness during the bout, but Page hardly stood out and ultimately lost the gold to the newly-formed trio of Swerve Strickland and The New Level. He has no obvious path forward outside of seeking a rematch for the belts, but the Trios title division isn't where he belongs long-term.

Page is among AEW's most popular performers and should be treated like an important attraction. Relegating him to the trios tag team division does very little to maximize his star power or lend any credibility to the titles if they're constantly changing hands.

Winner: Swerve Strickland and The New Level

All signs pointed to Swerve Strickland recruiting the former New Day in his pursuit of the AEW World Trios Championship, and sure enough, they walked away with the gold in their grasp.

Kofi and Austin Creed were languishing in WWE's tag team scene for the last year and wisely requested their release in May. AEW was the obvious landing spot for them, though the pairing with Strickland seems to benefit Strickland in the interim more than it does them.

Regardless, it was a simple use of all three men and already they have quality chemistry together. Although they're bigger than competing for the Trios titles, this win does put them in a prominent position to shine coming out of the event and they can continue to build on it going forward.

After spending so much time in WWE, The New Level are a breath of fresh air in AEW and came across as total stars in their two appearances at All In.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Kyle Fletcher saw his momentum cut short when he had to vacate the AEW TNT Championship earlier in the year due to an injury. However, he was able to pick up right where he left off by betraying Konosuke Takeshita upon his return and eventually unseating him for the AEW International Championship.

The build for the three-way between Fletcher, Takeshita and Kazuchika Okada heading into All In was well done with the three past and present members of The Don Callis Family members teasing tension. The match was entertaining as expected, but the outcome left a lot to be desired.

Okada regaining the gold was the least interesting outcome AEW could have gone with, as Takeshita ended his historic run at Double or Nothing. That should have led to Okada moving on up to the main event scene instead of continuing to tread water in the International title mix.

More importantly, Fletcher losing puts him right back to where he was: behind Okada in The Don Callis Family. A win would have been huge for him and defined what was shaping up to be a strong title run, but though he could still rebound if he too breaks away from the faction and embraces being a babyface.

MJF won the first-ever AEW All In main event three years, successfully defending the AEW World Championship against Adam Cole. He was involved in another marquee match the subsequent year with Will Ospreay and won last year's men's Casino Gauntlet match.

MJF is fresh off competing in the Casino Gauntlet for the second straight year, with the biggest difference this time being that he didn't emerge victorious. He had a strong showing by starting out with his rival Andrade El Idolo, but it largely felt like a waste of the three-time AEW World champion after dominating the AEW landscape prior to dropping the strap in early July.

Of course, he's still carrying around his custom title belt claiming that he's the uncrowned world champ, so it's more a matter of when than if he'll set his sights back on the gold. However, a one-on-one outing with Andrade at All In would have been a better use of both men and effectively furthered their feud.

The rest of the combatants were fine but overshadowed the more appealing story at hand with MJF and his appalling absence from the world championship conversation right now.

The Young Bucks' clash with Cope & Cage over the AEW World Tag Team Championship lived up to its dream match billing, but more shockingly, Cage & Cope managed to keep their title reign intact.

AEW has added so much depth to its tag team division in the last few months alone that keeping the belts on Cage & Cope was the right call so they can face a few more fresh teams before finally being beaten.

That alone was an exciting twist, but the visual of so many top tandems facing off afterward emphasized just how stacked the scene is at the moment. Cage & Cope, Young Bucks, FTR, The Motor City Machine Guns and The New Level are an incredible core to build around.

The many match possibilities can carry the tag title picture through the next six months at least and put more eyes on the twin titles than ever before. The division largely lost its luster a few years back but has been rejuvenated in a massive way coming out of All In.

Tag team wrestling is alive and well in AEW.

Loser: AEW Women's World Championship Picture

Whenever Willow Nighingale has ever won the big one, it hasn't been long after that she's lost it, and All In was unfortunately no exception.

It was only a month ago at Redemption that she dethroned Thekla for the AEW Women's World Championship, leaving Thekla without anything substantial to do at All In. On paper, Nightingale defending against women's Owen Hart Cup winner Mercedes Moné was the bigger match, but Thekla deserved to be involved in some capacity after carrying the division all 2026 long.

Instead, Thekla had to resort to sitting in the crowd watching Moné prematurely end Nightingale's championship reign. The matchup itself was largely great, but it ended the same way as Nightingale's Double or Nothing 2024 encounter with Moné over the TBS title.

Although Moné is more natural as a heel, her facing Thekla for the AEW Women's World Championship would have been the fresher match. It also would have made Moné's title win that much more monumental following Thekla's lengthy run as champ.

Nightingale returns to chase mode, Moné is finally where she should have been long ago, and Thekla is the odd woman out despite the hot momentum she had as recently as July.

It was an emotional homecoming for Will Ospreay in England as The Aerial Assassin came out on top in his epic battle with Kenny Omega as the new AEW World champion in front of his family and friends at All In.

The entrance alone cemented his status as the face of the franchise, and the match was nothing short of spectacular from both an in-ring and storytelling standpoint. Both men were exceptional, but Ospreay in particular proved why he's AEW's anointed one with how he persevered through the punishment and had an answer for everything Omega pulled out of his arsenal.

The moment had been a long time coming for Ospreay, who put pen to paper with the promotion almost three years ago but had never captured AEW World title until now. His victory was clean as it should have been and the interference from outside forces was thankfully kept to a minimum.

Ospreay leaving All In with the world title always appeared to be the endgame dating back to the beginning of the year, so how AEW decides to follow up will be crucial. This shouldn't be the peak of Ospreay's push but rather the beginning of what has the potential to be a thrilling run for him on top.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Date, ringwalk, UK time, undercard, venue, records & how to follow on the BBC
articles.summary: All you need to know about Katie Taylor's farewell fight against Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin on Saturday night.
articles.body:
After almost a decade as a professional boxer, Katie Taylor will call time on her career after her 27th and final bout on Saturday.

The Irish superstar, 40, will aim to become a three-time undisputed world champion against Frenchwoman Flora Pili in Dublin.

Taylor, who has won 25 professional fights and avenged her only defeat against Chantelle Cameron, will defend her light-welterweight WBO, WBA and IBF titles against Pili, who boasts an unbeaten 12-0 record.

With the vacant WBC title on the line, the Bray fighter has finally got her dream bout at Croke Park as 80,000 fans are expected to pack out the stadium.

Will Taylor claim a fairytale farewell on home soil? Or will 29-year-old Pili spoil the party and pull off a huge upset?

Here is all you need to know about Taylor v Pili.

Live text commentary will begin at 20:00 BST on the BBC Sport website and app.

You can also follow the action through fight week on BBC Sport via the 5 Live Boxing podcast.

Taylor and Pili are scheduled to make their ringwalks at about 22:10 .

All timings are estimated and subject to change.

Katie Taylor v Flora Pili - WBA, WBO, WBC & IBF light-welterweight world titles

Paddy Donovan v Tyrone McKenna - welterweight

Taylor Bevan v Emmet Brennan - super-middleweight

Joe McGrail v Matthew Boreland - super-bantamweight

Molly McCann v Sylwia Doligala - bantamweight

How do Taylor and Pili's records compare?

Following a decorated amateur career, which included winning gold at the 2012 Olympics, Taylor quickly established herself as a dominant force once turning professional in 2016.

Taylor claimed three stoppage wins in her first five professional bouts and landed her first world title in her seventh contest, claiming the vacant WBA lightweight belt, with a unanimous decision victory over Anahi Ester Sanchez in Cardiff.

The rest of Taylor's career has played out at the very highest level, competing across 20 successive world title bouts and winning 19 of them.

Defeat by Cameron, which Taylor avenged in their rematch, remains the only loss on her 26-fight record. Taylor has six victories via knockout.

Pili, 11 years younger than Taylor, has won all 12 of her fights as a professional - winning two by knockout.

Just two of her fights have taken place outside her native France, earning victories in Italy and Luxembourg.

A deserved Croke Park send-off for Irish star

There could hardly be a more fitting setting for Taylor's final fight. She has wanted to headline at Croke Park for years - and it promises to be a celebration of one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures.

Reports suggest many in attendance will be experiencing a live boxing event for the first time, underlining the extent of Taylor's influence beyond the sport.

When Taylor was growing up, females were not permitted to box in Ireland. She went on to become a trailblazer for the sport, winning Olympic gold at London 2012 and inspiring a generation of female fighters.

Her professional career has been equally remarkable. She has consistently broken new ground on the biggest stages.

Her trilogy with Amanda Serrano produced three landmark encounters, beginning with their first meeting at a sold-out Madison Square Garden in 2022. Their subsequent rematches were broadcast globally on Netflix, expanding the reach of women's boxing even further.

Taylor is already a two-weight undisputed world champion and aims to secure undisputed status for a third time in her farewell bout.

Mandatory challenger Pili has earned her opportunity and cannot be overlooked, but Taylor remains the consummate professional and will be determined to conclude her career on a high.

articles.title: Caroline Dubois calls Alycia Baumgardner a coward and challenges American to make biggest fight in women's boxing
articles.summary: Alycia Baumgardner described Caroline Dubois' performance against Amelia Moore as "lacklustre", before the British boxer criticised the American as a 'coward' for not showing up to her post-fight press conference ahead of a potential super-fight between the pair
articles.body:
The transatlantic rivals have been heavily-linked to a potential super-fight as Baumgardner prepares to step into the same division as Dubois when she challenges Elif Nur Turhan for the IBF lightweight world title on November 8.

Dubois was approached by a spectating Baumgardner at the ropes in the immediate aftermath of her unanimous decision win over Amelia Moore in Birmingham, a tug of war at the microphone and fierce war of words further fuelling their growing feud.

The Londoner later criticised Baumgardner's absence in her post-fight press conference.

"I'm surprised she isn't there. I think she's a coward," she said. "I wish she was here so I could say it to her face. I really do.

"I think she's a coward. I think she's a coward because she isn't here today. She should have come to the press conference. This is the biggest fight in women's boxing."

Baumgardner described the performance as "lacklustre" and insisted Dubois would need to "tighten up" were she to have a chance of beating the former undisputed world champion.

Dubois hit back by questioning Baumgardner's failure to secure fights against Katie Taylor and Claressa Shields, while explaining how she was "already better" than her at the age of 25.

"She's tried as hard as she can to dismiss me and make it seem like I'm not on her level, but I am," Dubois continued.

"I'm the world champion, and she's moving up to my division. Yeah, I think this is the biggest fight in women's boxing.

"I think it will be a great fight, and I hope that she wins against Elif [Nur Turhan], but you never know.

"Maybe it's Elif who wins, and it'll be me and her facing off, so let's not try and write off Elif."

Stephanie Han is another possible option for Dubois having just retained her WBA lightweight title in a majority decision win over Holly Holm.

"Nakisa [MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian] flew me out earlier this year to watch Stephanie fight against Holly Holm," said Dubois.

"I went to the press conference afterwards. I wasn't afraid to come to the press conference.

"I called her out openly there and then, and she promised me we would do it, that it is a fight that's going to happen, and I intend to hold her to that. I want to fight Stephanie."

Speaking to Sky Sports , MVP founder Jake Paul said they were "100 per cent ready to go when they want to sign the contracts" with regards to a fight between Dubois and Baumgardner.

It comes after Claressa Shields accused Baumgardner of being "scared" of Dubois, to which the American replied by calling her counterpart "jealous".

"Alycia is not scared of anyone, I know it's going to happen, she has to get through November 8 and then we can have those discussions," said Paul.

"I think it's funny when fans or critics say certain people are scared of somebody - they aren't scared, it's what they do for a living."

articles.title: Taylor-Pili: Maguire recalls his night on Ali's undercard
articles.summary: With Katie Taylor set to be the first boxer to headline Croke Park since Muhammad Ali beat Al 'Blue' Lewis in 1972, BBC Sport NI catches up with Paddy Maguire, who was last to box on that iconic night.
articles.body:
Croke Park's storied history contains some of Irish sport's most seminal moments.

Primarily a stadium for Gaelic games, there have been occasions when other sports graced the hallowed turf and on 19 July 1972, punches replaced points as Muhammad Ali took on Al 'Blue' Lewis.

When Katie Taylor makes her final career ringwalk on Saturday with the undisputed light-welterweight crown on offer against Flora Pili, 54 years will have passed since 'The Greatest' starred at the since redeveloped venue.

While Ali was the main attraction in 1972, it was Belfast's Paddy Maguire who boxed last on that balmy Wednesday evening, coming through on points against France's Guy Caudron.

"It's hard to believe it has taken so long for boxing to return to Croke Park," Maguire told BBC Sport NI.

As an amateur, Maguire won featherweight silver at the 1966 Commonwealth Games in Jamaica - a medal that was "hard won as they were all tough fights".

A switch to the professional code prompted another move, this time to London where he linked up with manager Paddy Byrne.

It was this relationship which ultimately led to Maguire and Pat McCormack earning a slot on Ali's undercard, which also featured Donegal's Paddy Doherty, plus future light-heavyweight world champion John Conteh and heavyweight Joe Bugner, who would twice lose to Ali in later years.

"Pat and myself were great friends and had the same manager, so it was great for us to be on such a huge bill," Maguire recalled.

"To be a man from the Kashmir Road in Belfast, fighting on Muhammad Ali's bill was great, but I could never understand why there were so few Irish fighters involved."

Meeting Ali a 'high point' for hurling icon Keher

Aged 30, Ali - who had iconic wins against George Foreman and Joe Frazier to come in his career - accepted a reported £300,000 offer by Kerry promoter Michael 'Butty' Sugrue to fight in Ireland.

Battling a cold, Ali secured an 11th-round victory over Lewis and while just 17,000 made their way through the turnstiles - 15,000 short of the break-even mark -others were more creative in how they entered.

One of those attending by conventional means was Kilkenny hurling great Eddie Keher in a year in which he collected the fourth of his six All-Ireland senior medals.

A boxing fan, Keher recalls burning the midnight oil in his youth with his father, tuning into radio commentary of heavyweight greats Joe Louis, Rocky Marciano and then Ali.

With the promotional push for Croke Park in full swing, an idea was hatched to have the pair meet at the Kilternan Hotel - "a high point" in his life.

"I was dumbstruck when I saw him [Ali]. He was different from what I imagined because he wasn't the flamboyant guy we'd seen on television," Keher told BBC Sport NI's GAA Social podcast.

"The press were outside and I had two hurls and a sliotar [ball]. I was supposed to teach him how to play hurling, but he was finding it hard to hit the ball with two hands, so he was hitting it with one hand like a tennis racquet.

"He was still the ordinary guy but then he came up close to me and said, 'we'll put on a show for these guys' so he went to hit me with his hurl and I put up mine to save me. Then he was going around fencing with the hurl and became the Muhammad Ali we knew."

While Keher and those in attendance remember the occasion with fondness, behind the scenes things were a little more chaotic.

Fight gloves had not been sourced, prompting a last-minute scramble to have some sent from England, resulting in a late start to the undercard which would ultimately leave Maguire waiting until after the main event before he boxed.

"There weren't too many left by that stage, but I ended up on last as I was seen as an exciting, all-action pressure fighter," Maguire reasoned.

"Maybe their idea was to have me on last to try and keep people there."

Maguire remembers Ali as a "lovely man" - and it would not be the last time the boxers' paths would cross.

After British and Commonwealth bantamweight title defeats, Maguire would avenge a previous loss against David Needham in 1975 to get his hands on the Lonsdale Belt - and in the build-up, reunited with Ali at Wembley.

In August 1977, they met again in the Grosvenor House Hotel for a testimonial in honour of Ali's friend Paddy Monaghan, the Fermanagh-born bare-knuckle boxer.

By then, Maguire had drawn with European champion Daniel Trioulaire, while a second crack at the title brought a loss to Franco Zurlo before defeat by Johnny Owen proved his final stand.

"There were ups and down," Maguire says of his career, "but it's one I'm proud of."

While his days in the ring were over, he would remain connected to the sport, serving as a member of the British Boxing Board of Control's Northern Ireland Council.

On Saturday, Maguire will watch from home as Taylor, a trailblazer for women's boxing, makes the same walk as Ali.

"I've had the opportunity to tell my kids and grandchildren about my time there, so for those boxing this time, they can do the same one day," he said.

"Katie Taylor has had a great career and deserves her big night, but hopefully it's not another 50 years before boxing's back in Croke Park."

articles.title: Mercedes Mone Reveals Major Injury Suffered in AEW Women's Title Win vs. Willow at All In
articles.summary: Mercedes Mone's celebration was slightly delayed after defeating Willow Nightingale to win the AEW Women's World Championship at All In on Sunday.
articles.body:
Mercedes Mone's celebration was slightly delayed after defeating Willow Nightingale to win the AEW Women's World Championship at All In on Sunday.

During the All In post-show press conference, Mone revealed that she was forced to see the doctor immediately after her match for stitches for a brutal injury suffered early in the contest.

"I haven't even had time to process winning this. I was so focused on taking Willow's smile and ending her career," Mone said (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News). "I finally get to look at the title because straight after the match, I had to go to the doctor to get stitches for my nose that she broke. ... Right at the f--king beginning."

Mone appeared to suffer the injury when Nightingale threw her face first into a guardrail.

Still, the 34-year-old fought through the pain and claimed the AEW women's title for the first time in her storied career. She acknowledged that Nightingale gave her a beating at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday, but she overcame the onslaught to come out on top.

"Me and Willow have had it out for each other since the day that we met. Today, all of our emotions, frustrations and history were right there in the ring," she said. "We gave it our all. She legit beat my ass all over the ring, but I beat her harder."

articles.title: “Once Khabib and Islam move on”: Dan Hooker targets Usman Nurmagomedov’s UFC debut with bold legacy challenge after PFL contract comes to an end
articles.summary: International Sports News: Dan Hooker is ready to welcome Usman Nurmagomedov to the UFC if the undefeated PFL champion makes the move. Hooker said he would enjoy beating a fight.
articles.body: Dan Hooker is ready to welcome Usman Nurmagomedov to the UFC if the undefeated PFL champion makes the move. Hooker said he would enjoy beating a fighter carrying one of MMA’s biggest family names. Usman finished his PFL contract with a first round win over Archie Colgan in July and is now in a 90 day exclusive negotiation period with the promotion. A UFC move is possible, but no deal has been confirmed.Dan Hooker wants Usman Nurmagomedov as UFC debut opponentHooker explained his thinking during an interview with Submission Radio. The New Zealander believes Usman could be heading toward the UFC, especially after his PFL contract ended while Islam Makhachev moved up from lightweight.For Hooker, however, this is not simply about welcoming another new fighter. He sees the Nurmagomedov name itself as part of the challenge.“Once Khabib and Islam move on, it was for Usman to come to the UFC. You know, it’s no coincidence that his PFL contract ended. Islam goes up, and Usman’s contract runs out,” Hooker said.He then explained why fighting Usman would mean so much to him.“It’s the legacy, yeah. That would be the exciting thing for me with that fight. Just, you know, we get another chance to stiffen the angle up, go up against the legacy.”Usman has plenty behind his name already. The 28 year old remains unbeaten and improved his professional record to 22-0 when he stopped Archie Colgan in the first round at PFL New York on July 31. That fight was the final bout on his existing PFL deal.The PFL has said Usman entered a 90 day exclusive negotiation window after that fight. So, while UFC talk is growing, his next move has not been decided yet.Hooker is also attracted to the idea of fighting Usman in his home country.“Going to a guy’s hometown and ruining his debut in his hometown, that puts a little fuzzy feeling in my stomach,” he said.Dan Hooker dismisses Ilia Topuria fight talkThere has also been talk of Usman possibly fighting Ilia Topuria if he joins the UFC. Hooker does not believe that makes sense.Speaking to Submission Radio, Hooker argued that Topuria would have too much to lose by facing an unranked fighter who has never competed in the UFC.“I saw outlandish ones that say people are like, ‘Oh, Usman’s going to come in and fight Ilia Topuria.’ Get f**ked, be serious!” Hooker said.He added that he believes other established lightweights may also avoid taking such a risky fight.For now, Hooker has his own job to handle. He is scheduled to face former KSW two division champion Salahdine Parnasse at UFC Paris on September 5. A win would give Hooker a stronger case if the UFC eventually signs Usman.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Health is wealth": Mike Perry breaks silence following Brandon Jenkins defeat and scary shoulder injury
articles.summary: International Sports News: Mike Perry has finally addressed what happened after a rough night in Orlando. “Platinum” headlined the first Duel Arena event on Saturday, but the fi.
articles.body: Mike Perry has finally addressed what happened after a rough night in Orlando. “Platinum” headlined the first Duel Arena event on Saturday, but the fight did not go anywhere near as planned. Brandon Jenkins, who stepped in on short notice, stopped Perry in the opening round. The fight had already taken a bad turn before the finish. During an exchange in the corner, Perry’s shoulder popped out of place. Jenkins immediately took advantage of the situation, leading to the stoppage and bringing Perry’s main event to an abrupt end.What Mike Perry said in his first statement after the lossPerry did not share a detailed breakdown of the fight itself. Instead, his first public message focused heavily on looking after his body and preparing for whatever comes next.On Monday, he posted on Twitter: “Health is wealth.”He then expanded on that idea, writing, “The MMA lifestyle taking care of the body, mind and spirit.” Perry also pointed toward the gym and the role of strength beyond fighting.His message was clear about what he thinks needs attention now: “Organize, be consistent, more recovery and stretching.”That sounds less like a post-fight excuse and more like a reset. Perry also said he was taking knowledge from the experience into his “future endeavors,” while making it clear he still has plenty left to work on.Why the Brandon Jenkins matchup happened in the first placePerry was not originally supposed to fight Jenkins. His scheduled opponent was Dillon Danis, but that matchup fell apart only two days before the event.That left Perry facing a completely different opponent in his hometown main event. Jenkins accepted the fight on short notice and ended up securing the stoppage win.For Perry, the result was a sharp change from his previous appearance. He entered Duel Arena 1 after a stoppage victory over Nate Diaz on the Rousey vs. Carano card in May.Perry’s message points toward recovery and future workRather than focusing on the loss, Perry’s statement centered on rebuilding. He talked about strength, consistency, recovery and stretching, while also saying there was “more to work for” and “more work to do.”The shoulder issue now becomes the immediate backdrop to that next chapter. articles.title: Gaethje y una posible revancha con Topuria: "La UFC tiene la última palabra"
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense ha revelado que no peleará hasta el año que viene, dejando en el aire su rival
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense ha revelado que no peleará hasta el año que viene, dejando en el aire su rival
articles.body: Justin Gaethje ha sido el mejor peleador de 2026 sin duda alguna. El estadounidense se ha reinventado de la mejor manera posible frenando el hype de Paddy Pimblett en enero para convertirse de nuevo en campeón interino y protagonizando posteriormente la mayor sorpresa del año tras finalizar a Ilia Topuria en el UFC Casa Blanca y cumplir su sueño de ser campeón indiscutido de peso ligero. El estadounidense ha confirmado que no volverá a competir hasta 2027 para tomarse un descanso, y ha dejado abierta la puerta a una posible revancha con 'El Matador'. Gaethje sigue afirmando que si de él dependiese Topuria no sería su siguiente rival, ya que según él no hizo méritos suficientes en el combate para obtener esa revancha inmediata. Sin embargo, 'The Highlight' sabe que él no tiene la última palabra, por lo que depende de la decisión que tome la UFC y lo que consideren mejor para su negocio, algo en lo que Justin no tiene voz alguna. En una entrevista con 'Sports Ilustrated', Gaethje ha reconocido que "la UFC es la que tiene la última palabra y la que toma la decisión final sobre mi siguiente rival, así que quién sabe. Yo no voy a pelear hasta el año que viene, y él tampoco querrá pelear hasta el año que viene para recuperarse de algunas lesiones. Quién sabe, aunque no siento que esa deba ser mi siguiente pelea", sentenció. Topuria todavía no se ha pronunciado públicamente al respecto desde su derrota más allá de un comunicado en Instagram, por lo que no se le espera de vuelta en el octágono hasta principios de 2027 como mínimo. 'El Matador' se está recuperando de las fracturas en la nariz y sus dos orbitales, además del golpe moral que supuso su primera derrota profesional y la manera en la que se produjo, así que los plazos de ambos concuerdan bastante para llevar a cabo una revancha cuando estén preparados. De hecho, a pesar de que Gaethje no tuvo lesiones aparentes ha revelado que "mi vida después del UFC Casa Blanca ha sido increíble, aunque tuve que hacer una recuperación en casa de tres semanas. De hecho, todavía no puedo golpear nada con ninguna de mis dos manos porque me duelen por culpa de la pelea. Voy a descansar durante el resto del año y a disfrutar con mi familia porque pelee dos veces durante los primeros seis meses del año y puse todo sobre el papel. Hablaré con mi familia, mi equipo y la gente que me quiere y confío que será honesta conmigo y tomaré una decisión". Por tanto, habrá que esperar unos meses para conocer el futuro inmediato tanto de Ilia como de Justin. Lo que está claro es que si el peleador estadounidense de 37 años sigue compitiendo y no se retira a corto plazo ambos caminos parecen destinados a encontrarse, aunque la siguiente derrota que tenga Gaethje probablemente significará su retirada tras haber conseguido todo lo que se propuso al inicio de su carrera.

articles.title: Dan Hooker willing to welcome Usman Nurmagomedov to UFC because 'no one else will'
articles.summary: Dan Hooker is no stranger to welcoming highly touted champions from other organizations.
articles.body:
Dan Hooker is no stranger to welcoming highly touted champions from other organizations.

Hooker (24-14 MMA, 14-10 UFC) was ex-Bellator champion Michael Chandler's octagon debut in 2021, but the fight didn't go his way. Now he draws former two-division KSW champion Salahdine Parnasse (23-2 MMA, 0-0 UFC) in Saturday's UFC Fight Night 287 ( Paramount+ ) main event at Accor Arena in Paris.

With rumblings of PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov (22-0) potentially joining the UFC, Hooker is willing to put his hand up for that fight, too.

"It's the same thing as when I fought Chandler. It's the same thing with this Parnasse guy," Hooker told Submission Radio . "It'll be the same thing with Usman. No one else will take the fight. ... You think Ilia Topuria 's going to take that risk of fighting an unranked non-UFC fighter? No one else wants to take the risk.

"It's the same reason why I was the guy to fight Chandler. It's the same reason why they're paying me money to fight Parnasse is because none of these other guys in the division want to risk it for the biscuit. So they call up Dan Hooker, they offer him a bit of danger money, and he welcomes these boys to the big leagues."

Hooker likes the position of spoiling someone's debut, and with Nurmagomedov, it'll have even more meaning.

"That would be the exciting thing for me with that fight is you would get another chance to step in there and go up against a legacy," Hooker said. "Going to a guy's hometown and ruining his debut, that puts a little fuzzy feeling in my stomach."

articles.title: Primer culpable por el asesinato de Tupac Shakur tras 30 años: ¿Por qué Tyson se sintió responsable?
articles.standfirst: Declaran culpable a Duane 'Keffe D' Davis por el asesinato de Tupac Shakur casi 30 años después
articles.summary: Declaran culpable a Duane 'Keffe D' Davis por el asesinato de Tupac Shakur casi 30 años después
articles.body: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis ha sido declarado culpable del asesinato en primer grado por organizar el tiroteo desde un vehículo que acabó con la vida del rapero Tupac Shakur hace 30 años. El fiscal sostuvo ante el jurado que Davis, junto a su sobrino Orlando Anderson y el resto de la su banda (Crips), decidió ir tras Shakur después del altercado que tuvo Anderson con el rapero en el hotel MGM Grand de Las Vegas. El veredicto ha sido de un jurado popular de Las Vegas formado por 16 personas y ahora deberá ser el juez el que determine la pena definitiva. El asesinato de Tupac Shakur en 1996 es uno de los crímenes para famosos y polémicos de la historia de la música. Duane 'Keffe D' Davis (63 años), la única persona enjuiciada por la muerte del legendario rapero de 25 años, se enfrenta un único cargo de asesinato con arma mortal, agravado por la intención de promover, fomentar o ayudar a una organización criminal. En noviembre de 2023 Davis se declaró inocente y desde entonces se mantuvo bajo custodia con una fianza de 750.000 dólares. En la promoción de sus memorias, publicadas en 2019, Duane 'Keffe D' Davis habló de la banda Crips, el papel de esta en la muerte del rapero y se autoproclamó como "uno de los pocos testigos presenciales vivos" de asesinato de Tupac Shakur. El 13 de septiembre de 1996 moría asesinado en un tiroteo Tupac Shakur, uno de los raperos más famosos de la historia (ha vendido más de 75 millones de discos) y todo un símbolo para una parte de la juventud afroamericana de Estados Unidos. Unos días antes Tupac acudió a un compate de su buen amigo Mike Tyson contra Bruce Seldon, y a la salida fue víctima de un tiroteo provocado por la mortal guerra que estaban manteniendo los raperos de la Costa Este y los de la Coste Oeste. El cantante no quiso perderse el estreno de una canción que había compuesto especialmente para la presentación del combate de su amigo. Tyson ganó a Seldon e invitó a Shakur a una gran fiesta para celebrar el combate... una fiesta a la que Tupac Shakur nunca acudió. "Me siento extremadamente culpable de su muerte, porque pienso que si él no hubiese acudido a mi combate nunca lo hubiesen tiroteado", se sinceró Tyson en la prensa estadounidense rompiendo su silencio sobre el asesinato de Tupac Shakur. En 2010 Tyson explicó en el reportaje 'One Night in Vegas: Tyson & Tupac' que su fuerte amistad con Tupac Shakur se cimentó en el pasado carcelario de ambos: "Cuando ingresé en prisión en 1992 (condenado por violación) todos los días me llamaba, me mandaba un mensaje o al menos lo intentaba". En 1995 el que ingresó en la cárcel fue Shakur y a partir de ese momento su amistad de tornó indestructible: "Los dos teníamos muchos problemas para encontrar gente en la que confiar". Aunque Tyson reconoce que nunca llegó a comprender completamente al carismático Shakur: "Era como un guerrero... Su corazón era tan grande como este planeta. Tenía mucho amor y compasión dentro del él, pero nunca se lo podías ver por culpa de su ira". Para mí es muy difícil hablar de esto. Tupac Shakur era un chaval que quería ser un genio... y lo consiguió", apuntó el 'Terror del Garden'. La creciente rivalidad entre los raperos de la Coeste Oeste y de la Costa Este pudo ser el motivo del asesinato no resuelto de Tupac Shakur. Uno de los sospechosos de asesinar al famoso rapero fue su amigo The Notorious B.I.G., que representaba a la Costa Este, mientras que Tupac era del Oeste. Seis meses después de la muerte de Tupac, en marzo de 1997, The Notorious B.I.G. moría tiroteado en Los Ángeles.
